motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain Citg, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.08, Form of Government and Section 2.15J20 Magor Pro Tempore and Council Assignments Councilmember Wood explained that the proposed ordinance, requested bg Councilmember Wright and himself, codifies Eagle Mountain Citg's six-member council form of government and establishes that the powers of municipal government are vested in the Citg Council, consisting of five Councilmembers and the Magor. The Citg Council shall make the decisions for the Citg with a vote and approval in an open and public meeting. The ordinance further clarifies the executive and staff powers and identifies that, on an annual basis, the Citg Council shall elect a Magor Pro Tempore from the bodg of the elected Citg Councilmembers and will discuss and make assignments for representation and support for the citizens of the Citg. Theg worked with the Citg Attorneg to ensure that the amendment clarified State Code rather than altering or removing authoritg from angone. Discussion ensued regarding the following: o Additional changes to the language in the amendment; . Concerns that, "2.O8.O30. Council Administration. No one member of the citg council or the magor shall make decisions for the citg council nor shall ang member of the citg council, knowinglg or otherwise, give the perception to an organization or individual citizen that theg represent the full bodg of the citg council without the citg council's vote and approval in an open and public meeting," could impede staff and the Magor from functioning in certain aspects of their roles or be misinterpreted, leading to accusations and possible punitive measures; . The desire to empower staff to explore all options and solutions without fear of retribution. o Changing 2.OB.060. Adoption of Policies to "No new policies, code, ordinance, or resolution shall be created andenacted bg magor or staff without written request and then consent of the majoritg vote of citg council in an open and public meeting;" . Confusion over the impact of the standards on the procurement code; o Wording differences between the amendment and State Code; o Benefits and complications should the Magor and Counciljointlg make liaison assignments; and . Add¡ng the process for nomination and approval of the Magor Pro Tempore to the proposed standards for claritg. Mr. Draper stated that the proposed changes to EMMC 2.08.030, while good in principle and practice, are an addition to, rather than a clarification of State statute and would constitute a substantive change to the law impacting the Magor's powers, duties, and functions thus necessitating certain procedural requirements to be followed when voting on the change. When the Magor speaks, unless he emphaticallg states that he is speaking for himself, others could assume he is speaking for the Citg as a whole. He recommended adding a section that the legislative intent is to codifg and clarifg existing standards rather than to make substantive changes

motions.headline: Less water required from builders for new homes
motions.summary: The city cut the water rights developers must turn over per new home, dropping the indoor requirement from 0.53 to 0.34 acre-feet, and ordering a study of apartment water use.
motions.impact: This lands on developers, not on your water bill. It follows the city's smaller lawn requirements, so new yards will have less sod. The council also wants a closer look at how much water apartments actually use.

motions.headline: Council rules rewrite delayed to February
motions.summary: The council put off an ordinance spelling out the powers of the mayor, council and staff, sending it back to the city attorney for rewording before February 6.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents. This is an internal rulebook about who at city hall can speak or decide for the city, and the debate returns February 6.
